detail.abstract: Accurately delineating natural park boundaries is essential for environmental policy evaluation. Standard national spatial datasets omit individual park names, whereas municipal open data often embed critical metadata within nested XML tags, causing attribute loss during standard GIS ingestion. This study developed an automated hybrid data engineering pipeline that integrates geospatial processing using sf and low-level XML parsing using xml2. Three fragmented municipal KML datasets from Gifu Prefecture—an ecologically critical region encompassing the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Shirakawa-mura—were integrated into a single, unified spatial infrastructure. By front-loading the parsing and integration steps upstream, the processed dataset was serialized into an optimized R Data Serialization (RDS) format, reducing file size by 71.6% and shortening loading time by a factor of 22 relative to parsing the raw KML files at runtime. To maximize interoperability, standalone GeoPackage and CSV formats with representative coordinates were generated. The dataset is supported by an online interactive Shiny web simulator (https://moteki.shinyapps.io/gifu-naturalparks-E/). All associated code, pipelines, and data outputs are permanently archived on Zenodo to ensure complete computational reproducibility. By providing an immediately deployable, name-attributed spatial infrastructure for natural park regulatory zones, this dataset is intended to support evidence-based environmental governance and sustainable land-use policy for ecologically sensitive regions.

title: The Covariant Economy: Riemannian Game Theory, Geodesic Utility, and the Topological Resolution of Macroeconomic Friction

detail.title: The Covariant Economy: Riemannian Game Theory, Geodesic Utility, and the Topological Resolution of Macroeconomic Friction
detail.abstract: Classical economic models-including the Nash Equilibrium and the Arrow-Debreu General Equilibrium-are mathematically restricted, flat-space (Euclidean) approximations of a continuously deformable economic reality. By mapping multi-agent interactions onto a dynamically tilting, κ-weighted Riemannian manifold, we establish the Covariant Subgame Perfect Equilibrium. We demonstrate mathematically that market frictions, monopolistic inefficiencies, and "irrational" behavioral deviations (such as the Winner's Curse) are not systemic errors, but the exact geodesic traversals of rational agents operating under the covariant curvature of asymmetric market mass. Furthermore, by introducing the Guardian Model, we prove that the Tragedy of the Commons is an artifact of Euclidean geometry; under sufficient macroeconomic mass, global cooperation emerges not as a moral imperative, but as a topological inevitability.

title: Institutional Logics in China's Rural Solar Transition and their Impacts on Energy Justice for Vulnerable Communities
affiliations: Beijing Forestry University, Beijing Forestry University, Colorado State University and Independent

detail.title: Institutional Logics in China's Rural Solar Transition and their Impacts on Energy Justice for Vulnerable Communities
detail.abstract: In the context of global climate mitigation, low carbon energy transitions have become central to sustainable development. However, while pursuing environmental objectives, such transitions may also reshape patterns of resource distribution and participation through institutional arrangements, generating new forms of inequality across distributive, procedural, and recognition dimensions. China, as the world's largest developing country and a major carbon emitter, provides an analytically rich context for examining how low carbon transitions intersect with equity concerns. This study investigates three photovoltaic projects in China: the Tengger Desert New Energy Base in Ningxia, the Dezhou Rooftop PV Program in Shandong, and the Yancheng Solar-Fishery Integration Project in Jiangsu. Drawing on field interviews and policy document analysis, the study employs a thematic grounded coding approach to develop a four dimensional analytical framework covering spatial entitlements, revenue distribution, technological adaptation, and policy design. The findings show that vulnerable rural communities often face constrained spatial rights, limited benefit sharing, uneven adaptive capacity, and restricted participation in top down governance processes. Based on this analysis, the paper develops policy recommendations to enhance institutional inclusiveness, optimize benefit-sharing mechanisms, and strengthen local governance capacity. These insights provide both theoretical contributions to the study of energy justice and practical references for promoting equitable and sustainable energy transitions in the Global South.

title: The Insurance Value of Income-Contingent Loans and the Borrower's Optimal Consumption and Investment
affiliations: University of Western Ontario, Australian National University (ANU), Australian National University (ANU) and Australian National University (ANU)

detail.title: The Insurance Value of Income-Contingent Loans and the Borrower's Optimal Consumption and Investment
detail.abstract: An income-contingent loan ties repayments to a borrower’s income and transfers part of the risk of low post-graduation earnings from the borrower to the lender. We study this risk-sharing arrangement in a continuous-time life-cycle model in which a graduate who holds an income-contingent loan chooses consumption, an investment strategy for a liquid account and a separate retirement account, and the rate at which income is contributed to the retirement account. The market is complete, and we solve the model by the martingale method, obtaining closed-form consumption and investment policies. In a calibration to an Australian graduate, the value of the repayment risk borne by the lender is about 19 percent of the loan and is concentrated among borrowers with low income and high debt. Relative to a traditional loan with the same expected present value of repayments, the income-contingent loan lowers the probability that the borrower exhausts liquid resources for those same borrowers and holds the repayment burden steadier across income states. The optimal rate of contribution to the retirement account is small for a risk-averse borrower, so the borrower keeps most resources liquid while the loan is outstanding. The findings quantify the insurance embedded in income-contingent lending and inform both the design of student-loan repayment and the financial decisions of borrowers who hold such loans.

title: When The Crowd Takes Control: Analysis of Crowd Behaviour and Stock Market Bubbles, Focus on AI Bubbles
affiliations: University of Rouen

detail.title: When The Crowd Takes Control: Analysis of Crowd Behaviour and Stock Market Bubbles, Focus on AI Bubbles

detail.abstract:
This paper analyses the influence of crowd behaviour on the formation and bursting of financial bubbles, drawing on the insights of behavioural finance. Unlike classical theories that assume investor rationality, numerous historical events have shown that emotions, cognitive biases, and social dynamics can lead to speculative excesses and a disconnection between asset prices and fundamentals.

 

This research adopts both a qualitative and quantitative approach. It examines emblematic cases such as the dot-com bubble, the cryptocurrency frenzy, and the GameStop phenomenon to illustrate how irrational collective behaviour can significantly influence financial markets. A contemporary analysis is then conducted on the artificial intelligence (AI) sector to assess the hypothesis of an ongoing speculative bubble, by studying prices, valuation ratios, media attention, and volatility.

 

The results suggest that some AI-related companies exhibit strong speculative dynamics, although the phenomenon is not widespread across the entire sector. This work thus highlights the importance of better understanding herd behaviour in finance. It also emphasizes the role of educational, regulatory, and technological tools in mitigating the risks associated with crowd-driven behaviours in financial markets.

title: When Passive Income Should Act As Active Income: A Dynamic Trigger Framework for Physical and Mental Incapacity, Structural Vulnerability, and Time-Poverty Through Parallel Phase Accumulation
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: When Passive Income Should Act As Active Income: A Dynamic Trigger Framework for Physical and Mental Incapacity, Structural Vulnerability, and Time-Poverty Through Parallel Phase Accumulation

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No known competing interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable.
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding.

detail.abstract: Passive income is commonly analysed as a means of wealth accumulation, retirement preparation, or financial independence. Less attention has been given to its possible design as a structured substitute for active labour income when earning capacity is interrupted before conventional retirement. This paper develops a conceptual framework in which financial, intellectual, and digital assets are accumulated in parallel with active labour during periods of relatively high capacity and are recharacterised as supplementary income following a qualifying vulnerability event. The proposed Dynamic Trigger Framework differs from a conventional age-based retirement model by linking activation to certified physical or mental incapacity, widowhood or acute structural displacement, and severe time-poverty associated with childbirth or caregiving. A related but distinct extension considers independently held passive assets as a continuous source of autonomy and intra-household bargaining power for women outside paid employment. The framework draws on life-cycle and permanent-income theory, human capital theory, disability economics, household finance, pension economics, time-poverty research, and household bargaining models. It is presented as a conceptual framework and interdisciplinary research agenda intended to stimulate empirical validation rather than prescribe immediate policy adoption. The paper specifies design conditions, implementation risks, testable propositions, and a pathway for future formal modelling and longitudinal validation. The framework is explicitly supplementary to state welfare, social insurance, pensions, and disability protection, and is principally relevant where institutional coverage is absent, incomplete, delayed, or inaccessible.

title: Motivating Job Seekers. A Field Experiment
affiliations: Ghent University - Department of Economics, Swedish Public Employment Service, Ghent University - Department of Personnel Management, Work and Organizational Psychology, Swedish Public Employment Service and

detail.title: Motivating Job Seekers. A Field Experiment
detail.abstract: Reduced motivation over the unemployment spell may contribute to declining job-finding rates. We report findings from a low-cost digital intervention that uses motivational emails to enhance job seekers' search effort. Using a randomized controlled trial that included 200,720 newly unemployed job seekers in Sweden, we evaluate both supportive messages aimed at encouraging inner motivation, and controlling messages focused on internal and external pressure. The messages increased compliance with mandatory activity reporting, indicating a clear first-stage behavioral response. However, this behavioral change did not translate in more effective job search as both types of emails caused a moderate but significant reduction in search effort and job finding. The supportive messages reduced the number of job applications and showed weakly negative job-finding effects, particularly among men. The controlling messages slightly backfired for job seekers who report strong autonomous motivation at the onset of unemployment. These findings underscore the challenges of motivating job seekers to actively search for jobs and suggest that low-cost digital interventions, in isolation, are inadequate and may even be counterproductive.

title: Persistence in Remittances: Evidence from Africa and Latin America
affiliations: University of Navarra - Department of Economics, Brunel University London - Department of Economics and Finance,  and

detail.title: Persistence in Remittances: Evidence from Africa and Latin America
detail.abstract: This paper uses fractional integration methods to estimate the degree of persistence of annual real remittances per capita to 21 Sub-Saharan African (SSA) and 12 Latin American and Caribbean (LAC) countries using data from World Bank World Development Indicators covering the period from 1980 to 2024. The results reveal substantial heterogeneity across both regions. In Sub-Saharan Africa, 5 (Kenya, Senegal, Benin, South Africa and Cameroon) of 21 countries show statistically significant mean reversion, whilst three others (Somalia, Côte d’Ivoire and Tunisia) display explosive persistence. In Latin America and the Caribbean, only the Dominican Republic and Panama display mean reversion. These findings shed light on whether shocks have transitory or permanent effects and therefore have crucial implications for the design of appropriate stabilization and development policies.

title: Open Fiscal Infrastructure for Mature Societies: A Reproducible Data Pipeline for Benchmarking Japanese Local Government Finances

detail.abstract: Objective comparative analysis using peer municipalities is fundamental to the evaluation of local public finance in Japan, and the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications publishes an official Similar Municipality Classification for this purpose. It remains that the underlying settlement statistics are distributed as complex Excel files optimized for visual readability and separated by municipal type, obstructing machine readability and leaving the classification largely untested against comprehensive national data. This study first constructs a reproducible data integration pipeline in R that resolves encoding conflicts, purges layout noise through dynamic anchor scanning, and disambiguates 25 duplicate municipality names via unique local government codes, yielding an integrated master dataset covering all 1,741 Japanese local governments for FY2024. Using this dataset, the study then asks whether the official classification delivers the internal homogeneity that benchmarking presupposes. Variance decomposition shows a pronounced gradient: the classification accounts for 55.2% of the variance in the financial capability index but only 29.1% for the ordinary balance ratio, 20.8% for the real debt service ratio, and 8.1% for the future burden ratio. Twenty-five of 28 peer groups exhibit a group mean below the 95% rigidity threshold while containing members above it. Subdividing peer groups by population density reduces within-group variance in fiscal capacity by 14.3% against a placebo of 1.4%, corroborating past geographical critiques of size-based classification, yet the same subdivision leaves expenditure rigidity unchanged. Fiscal capacity seems to be structurally determined, whereas fiscal stress is largely municipality-specific. These findings indicate that peer-group averages are insufficient for detecting fiscal distress, motivating thus the implementation of the interactive, municipality-level benchmarking application released with this dataset.

title: Firms as Foragers
affiliations: Universitat Pompeu Fabra/CREI and University of Cambridge

detail.title: Firms as Foragers
detail.abstract: We develop a theory of growth in which firms forage in idea space. A firm exploits a patch of related ideas, gradually exhausting opportunities for quality improvement, and then searches for a new patch. We cast this explore-exploit tradeoff as a tractable optimal-stopping problem and embed it in an endogenous-growth model. The composition of innovation — improving existing ideas versus discovering new ground — emerges as an equilibrium object. To construct an empirical representation of the idea space, we apply natural language processing to patent text data. The data support the theory’s central premises: returns to local exploitation diminish; firms stay longer on richer patches; and entry into new patches yields more and better patents. We calibrate the model to U.S. data and establish two results, on the composition of growth and on its pace. First, at a twenty-year horizon, patenting in new clusters accounts for over half of growth from quality improvements: sustained growth rests on firms continually entering new territory. Second, the model sign-identifies the origins of the productivity slowdown of the last four decades: exploitation spells have not shortened, weighing against worsening exploitation and tentatively pointing to harder exploration.

title: Preference Shocks and Policy Responses to Transition Risk
affiliations: Georgia State University, Georgia State University - Department of Economics and

detail.title: Preference Shocks and Policy Responses to Transition Risk
detail.abstract: Central banks and financial surveillance authorities need to cope with the potential realization of financial stability risks, adopting preventive measures or using liquidity once crises materialize. Transition risk — the stability risk associated with decarbonization — is a case in point. Such risk not only comes from policy changes, but also from preference shocks. Hence, this paper develops an environmental DSGE model with financial frictions and examines responses to shocks, including a novel angle on preference shocks. We show that these market-driven transition shocks generate larger macro-financial instability than carbon pricing for a given change in emissions, while delaying environmental gains. We then compare policy responses according to their timing. Ex-ante macroprudential policies that reduce banks’ exposure to transition risk dampen financial amplification, whereas ex-post interventions, such as quantitative easing, provide only partial stabilization once losses have materialized. Overall, our results indicate that market-led adjustments to transition risk are more destabilizing than carbon pricing, whereas preventive financial measures limit macro-financial instability more effectively than ex-post interventions under the policy comparisons considered, supporting the case for early action.

title: Geometry of Institutional Power: A Hodge-Theoretic Decomposition of Social Power Structures

detail.title: Geometry of Institutional Power: A Hodge-Theoretic Decomposition of Social Power Structures
detail.abstract: Political theory describes institutions as "structures of power" but rarely measures the structure. Following Dahl (1957), we record social power as a column-stochastic determination matrix : entry P ij is the share of agent j's conduct that agent i determines. The normalization produces a conserved quantity-power-over-so every claimed gain has a traceable source. The net power between each pair then admits a unique orthogonal split, the combinatorial Hodge decomposition of Jiang et al. (2011): a gradient part that ranks the agents (hierarchy) and a cyclic part that no ranking can represent (the circulating dominance of faction and coup). Their squared-norm shares satisfy H + C = 1, giving every structure a computable hierarchy index; three further coordinates-density, reciprocated determination, and algebraic connectivity-separate qualities ordinary language conflates, distinguishing a firm from a family and a junta from a triumvirate. A worked five-agent firm computes every coordinate and prices the influence a worker gains from an upward channel (Hirschman's voice). Applied to real faculty-hiring networks, the decomposition recovers known departmental prestige orders from placement counts alone, and shows these systems to be hierarchical in the direction of flow but substantially cyclic in its magnitude-structure a ranking alone conceals. Dynamically, if rule revision favors the already-powerful, the hierarchy share is a bounded submartingale: it converges to full hierarchy or none, with the probability of full hierarchy at least the hierarchy already standing; balanced factional cycles are unstable (the triumvirate resolves); and rich-get-richer revision forces a power-law tail. We provide a measurement protocol using existing data-labor-market monopsony, media concentration, differential policy responsiveness-and state the conditions under which the model is false.

title: Macro Announcement Days and Cumulative Asset-Price Changes in Türkiye
affiliations: Sabanci University

detail.title: Macro Announcement Days and Cumulative Asset-Price Changes in Türkiye
detail.abstract: Do a small number of scheduled announcement days account for a large share of longrun asset-price changes? Recent U.S. evidence shows that yield changes inside a three-day window around scheduled Federal Reserve meetings add up to the entire secular decline in long-term interest rates. We ask whether the same calendar logic holds in Türkiye, a high-inflation emerging market, using daily data on Borsa Istanbul equity indices and twoand ten-year government-bond yields over the 2010-2026 period. Transplanting the U.S. design mechanically fails: three-day windows around Monetary Policy Committee meetings contain almost none of the cumulative equity appreciation and move against the secular rise in nominal yields. Yet identical windows around consumer-price-index (CPI) releases account for roughly one third of cumulative equity appreciation and two thirds of the increase in the ten-year government-bond yield. This finding reveals a common repricing clock: in Türkiye, realized inflation releases, rather than monetary-policy meetings, mark the dates most closely associated with long-run equity appreciation and nominal-yield increases.

title: Beyond Current News: A Momentum-Augmented Model of Future Volatility
affiliations: University of Agder - School of Business and Law

detail.title: Beyond Current News: A Momentum-Augmented Model of Future Volatility
detail.abstract: We develop a novel, parsimonious, and interpretable volatility-forecasting framework that transforms 12-month Momentum from a return-history signal into a nonlinear state variable for future risk. The proposed Momentum-Augmented Realized Volatility models extend standard realized-volatility specifications by adding linear and quadratic Momentum terms while retaining controls for volatility persistence, current innovation magnitude, and downside asymmetry. The central innovation is the Momentum Impact Curve, a new graphical representation of how the accumulated medium-term return state affects future volatility. Whereas the conventional News Impact Curve varies current news while holding the broader state fixed, the Momentum Impact Curve varies Momentum while holding current volatility and the current innovation fixed. Using the U.S. market and size, value, and industry portfolios, we document a robust U-shaped relation: future volatility is highest after negative Momentum, lowest after moderately positive Momentum, and rises again after exceptionally strong positive Momentum. Across 21 return series, Momentum-augmented models dominate standard benchmarks in both insample selection and recursive out-of-sample forecasting.

title: Integrating Agentic Generative AI, Remote Work, and Psychological Theories of Teams to Strengthen US Financial Organizational Competitiveness

detail.abstract: The rapid transformation of work environments has established virtual and hybrid work as permanent fixtures, while simultaneously thrusting artificial intelligence (AI) from a tool into the role of an active agent. This paper presents a comprehensive, theoretical synthesis of these two paradigm shifts by examining how agentic generative AI can be strategically integrated to enhance remote and hybrid team effectiveness. We use the financial services sector as a rich, contextual case due to its unique challenges of security, regulation, and traditional culture. By merging Tuckman's seminal model of team development with emerging research on Human-AI Teaming (HAIT), we propose a unified framework to understand how AI influences team formation, conflict resolution, norm establishment, and high-performance execution. The analysis reveals that successful integration requires leveraging AI for cognitive and routine tasks while preserving and amplifying critical human elements such as emotional intelligence, psychological safety, and inclusive leadership. Drawing on recent empirical studies and industry examples from banking and fintech, this paper argues that the future of effective organizations lies not in choosing between human and AI capabilities, but in designing symbiotic teams where the whole is greater than the sum of its parts. The findings provide practical guidance for leaders navigating the complexities of AI integration in the evolving workplace.

title: The Sound of Streaming: Globalization and Acoustic Convergence in Popular Music Markets
affiliations: Ifo Institute and

detail.title: The Sound of Streaming: Globalization and Acoustic Convergence in Popular Music Markets
detail.abstract: Popular music reflects and shapes cultural dynamics, yet research on trends in music over long periods has focused almost exclusively on lyrics. We analyze diachronic trends in eight Spotify audio features (danceability, energy, loudness, speechiness, acousticness, instrumentalness, liveness, and valence) for the most popular songs in the United States (Billboard Hot 100) and Germany (GfK Entertainment Charts) from 1977 to 2025. Both markets exhibit broadly parallel trajectories: a steady decline in valence, an increase in loudness followed by a reversal in the streaming era, and a pattern of decline and subsequent recovery in acousticness. A decomposition at the level of genres reveals that the reversal in loudness and the decline in valence operate within genres rather than reflecting compositional shifts. We find that synchronization of audio features across the two countries, measured through rolling correlations of weekly series in first differences, has increased substantially since the middle of the 2010s, coinciding with the dominance of digital streaming platforms. This synchronization is strongest for features related to production and weakest for features that depend on language. Decomposing the effect, we show that the increase is driven both by a growing overlap in charted repertoire and by a genuine acoustic convergence among songs exclusive to one country, suggesting that streaming platforms synchronize national music markets through both a direct repertoire channel and an indirect aesthetic channel.

detail.abstract: We propose major amendments to the standard approach for retrieving valuations for U.S. patents from stock market data put forth by Kogan et al. (2017). For most firms, especially since the 1980s, grant events involve multiple, simultaneously issued patents. We argue that the number of simultaneously issued patents affects the signal-to-noise ratio used for filtering patent value estimates out of stock returns. We also propose a method for allocating the firm's capital gain from a week's multiple patent grants to individual patents. We show that our revised values exhibit much higher correlations with external value measurements.

detail.abstract: Organizations adopting artificial intelligence face a measurement problem: conventional human-capital indicators-educational attainment, training expenditure, tenure-describe credentials and inputs rather than the capabilities that determine whether AI adoption translates into productivity. Building on the braincapital research program initiated by Smith and colleagues (2021) and the OECD Neuroscience-inspired Policy Initiative, this paper develops an organization-level measurement framework for brain capital in an AI-intensive production environment. The framework makes three moves. First, it operationalizes organizational brain-capital stock through five pillars-cognitive capability, socio-emotional capability, psychological health, AI fluency, and learning and renewal-each specified in an indicator dictionary that favors observable behavior over self-report. Second, it distinguishes brain-capital stock from brain-capital conversion, modeling realized performance as a function of the interaction between brain-capital stock, deployed AI capability, and organizational work design, drawing on O-ring production theory, the economics of complementarities, and productivity J-curve evidence. Third, it derives falsifiable propositions-including that a multiplicative human-AI-organization specification explains performance variance beyond an additive specification-and sets out an estimable interaction model, a pilot protocol, and explicit criteria under which the framework should be revised or rejected. No empirical validation is claimed: the paper is presented as a measurement-development protocol rather than an empirical study. Its contribution is a narrower, testable, AI-era operationalization of brain capital for organizational research and future empirical work. Limitations and ethical constraints on individual-level use are discussed.

title: Risk-Managed Time-Series Momentum in Crypto Majors: Crash-State De-Risking and Drawdown Control

detail.title: Risk-Managed Time-Series Momentum in Crypto Majors: Crash-State De-Risking and Drawdown Control
detail.abstract: We study a fixed-lookback (L = 30 day) long/cash time-series-momentum (TSMOM) sleeve on liquid crypto-majors (BTC, ETH, BNB, XRP, ADA, SOL, DOGE), overlaid with a market-drawdown-state de-risking rule. The construction follows Moskowitz, Ooi and Pedersen (2012): hold each asset only while its trailing 30-day cumulative log-return is positive, otherwise rotate that allocation to cash; then scale the whole book's gross exposure down (×0.5) when the aggregate crypto market is more than 15% off its trailing peak. The headline finding is a drawdown-control result, not an alpha result. Across an offline 96-configuration grid, 100% of configurations produced a smaller maximum drawdown than equal-weight buy-and-hold; in an out-of-sample (OOS) walk-forward test with the lookback fixed a priori at L = 30, the sleeve delivered net-of-25bps Sharpe 1.41 (Harvey-Liu-Zhu t = 3.21) versus buy-and-hold Sharpe 0.70 (t = 1.60), with maximum drawdown cut roughly in half (-44.6% vs-84.4%). Adding the drawdown-state de-risk overlay (×0.5 beyond 15% off-peak) further reduced maximum drawdown to about-28% and lifted Calmar from roughly 1.56 to 1.98 while holding Sharpe near 1.53 (t = 3.69). The effect survives a frozen long-history (survivorshiphardened) universe and a 50bps round-trip cost assumption. We are explicit that this is risk-managed β-a documented trend premium with crash protection-not market-neutral alpha; that vol-targeting / Kelly sizing on top of this sleeve was tested and SETTLED NULL (it de-levers the payoff engine); that the L = 30 optimum is a recorded, accepted sharp-parameter fragility; that absolute returns are survivorship-inflated; and that the forward Harvey t > 3 promotion bar has NOT yet been cleared (the sleeve is paper-only and forward-accruing).

detail.abstract: Crop residue burning, most visibly the seasonal burning of paddy stubble ('parali') across Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh, exemplifies a textbook negative production externality: a private, near-zero-cost method of field clearance that imposes a large, geographically diffuse social cost through air pollution, respiratory illness, and greenhouse gas emissions. This paper undertakes a systematic economic evaluation of crop residue management in India, examining four linked dimensions: the scale of residue generation and burning; the documented economic and health costs of the status-quo practice of open burning; the economics of in-situ management alternatives, principally residue-incorporating seeding machinery deployed under the Centre's Crop Residue Management Scheme; and the economics of ex-situ, income-generating models that convert residue into a marketable input, including compressed biogas under the SATAT scheme, biomass briquettes and pellets, and the wider GOBARdhan circular-economy programme. Independent estimates place the annual health and economic cost of crop-burning-linked air pollution across Punjab, Haryana and Delhi at approximately USD 30 billion, alongside 44,000 to 98,000 estimated premature deaths nationally per year from agricultural residue burning, figures that stand in stark contrast to the machinery-subsidy and infrastructure investment of a few thousand crore rupees disbursed to date under India's principal residue-management policy instruments. The review finds that credible, farm-level cost-reducing and revenue-generating alternatives to burning exist and are documented in the literature, but that their large-scale adoption remains constrained by feedstock aggregation costs, machinery under-utilisation, and a persistent gap between the externality's true social cost and the price signals currently facing individual farmers. The paper closes with a comparative cost-benefit synthesis and policy recommendations for closing this gap.

title: Echoes Across the Divide: Incivility and the Fragmentation of Issue Publics in Immigration Discourse
affiliations: Syracuse University and University of Southern California - Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism

detail.title: Echoes Across the Divide: Incivility and the Fragmentation of Issue Publics in Immigration Discourse
detail.abstract: As immigration remains one of the most polarizing issues in U.S. politics, public discourse around it has become increasingly uncivil, especially on social media. This longitudinal study examines how incivility spreads and escalates across ideologically opposed issue publics on X. Drawing on conflict spiral theory, we conceptualize incivility as both a symptom and a driver of deepening conflict between pro-and antiimmigration publics. Additionally, we consult insights from research on networked publics and networked social influence to understand how online interactions shape the diffusion of hostile rhetoric. Using largescale X data, we deploy large language models to classify users' immigration stances and measure linguistic incivility. We also construct dynamic mention networks and apply graph-based machine learning to trace how incivility spreads over time and across ideological boundaries. The findings illuminate how conflict dynamics manifest through group network structures and how networked interactions spread incivility across groups with different immigration stances.

detail.abstract: Public sector banks (PSBs) in India underwent major institutional transformation after 2014. The Reserve Bank of India's Asset Quality Review, successive recapitalisations, the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (2016), large-scale bank consolidations (particularly 2019-2020), accelerated digitalisation, and a stronger orientation toward performance targets and cross-selling reshaped both balance sheets and day-today work. Financial results improved markedly: the gross non-performing asset (GNPA) ratio of PSBs fell from elevated levels of 9-14% in the late 2010s to approximately 2.58% by March 2025, while most banks returned to sustained profitability [1, 2]. Parallel to these gains, evidence of occupational stress and burnout among employees has accumulated. A 2024 cross-sectional study of bank employees in Kerala (majority public-sector) found moderate-to-high burnout in 82.2% of participants and mild-to-extremely severe stress in 26.2%; longer daily working hours were significantly associated with both outcomes [3]. Staff strength in PSBs declined from a peak near 850,000-857,000 around FY 2016-17 to roughly 746,000-756,000 by FY 2023-24, with a modest recovery to approximately 757,600 in FY 2024-25 [1]. Recurrent stressors identified across academic studies and employee-organisation accounts include role overload, performance-target intensity, staffing constraints relative to expanding responsibilities, technostress, customer pressure, and work-life conflict [3-7]. Union estimates of more than 500 employee suicides over roughly a decade circulate widely; official National Crime Records Bureau statistics contain no dedicated banking occupational category, and a circulating case compilation lists fewer verified reports [8-10]. This paper synthesises peer-reviewed studies, RBI employment and asset-quality data, parliamentary disclosures, and documented organisational responses. It concludes that the pressures are primarily structural and recommends improved staffing norms, realistic target calibration, confidential mental-health support, and clearer working-hour regulation.

title: Beyond Behavioural Fixes: Situating Personal Finance within Structural Political Economy
affiliations: Sri Lanka Institute of Information Technology

detail.title: Beyond Behavioural Fixes: Situating Personal Finance within Structural Political Economy
detail.abstract: This paper critically examines the intersection of behavioural finance strategies and structural political economy, drawing on interdisciplinary literature from behavioural economics, psychology, and development studies. While behavioural interventions such as automation, temporal framing, and crisis playbooks have demonstrated efficacy in reducing cognitive load and enhancing household resilience their applicability remains constrained by systemic inequalities, income volatility, and institutional gaps. Through qualitative desk research and critical documentary analysis, the study situates seven science-backed financial strategies within broader socio-cultural narratives and geopolitical contexts. Findings highlight the limitations of framing financial precarity as individual pathology, emphasizing instead the need for integrated approaches that combine behavioural insights with structural reforms. By foregrounding the Sri Lankan context alongside global debates, the paper contributes to contemporary scholarship on financial resilience, inequality, and the social construction of economic behaviour.

title: Elevating Saya: Integrating Mundhumi Soul-Consciousness into Public Health and Modern Stress Interventions

detail.title: Elevating Saya: Integrating Mundhumi Soul-Consciousness into Public Health and Modern Stress Interventions
detail.abstract:
The modern 21st century has reached the peak of technology and material prosperity, but ironically! The human mind is at its most stressful and turbulent point in history. The World Health Organization (WHO) has recently declared mental health a significant public health problem worldwide.

Modern psychiatry is frequently concerned with brain chemistry and biological abnormalities and overlooks the social, cultural, and environmental context of the person.

A medical anthropological approach to the study of illness, health, and disease suggests that illness and disease experiences are deeply connected to culture, lifestyle, and identity of individuals (Singer & Baer, 2011). The Mundhumi philosophy has been in practice for a very long time among the Kirat community of Nepal, a very rich, original, and indigenous knowledge system for understanding and dealing with mental stress, anxiety, and depression.

'Saya: Mundhumi Consciousness and Stress Management' is more than a cultural ritual; it is a strong base in public health, health psychology, and anthropology.

With a hectic and stressful life in the 21st century, it is not possible to remain in a state of complete health with just chemical pills and medicines. People can achieve inner peace only when they feel a bond with their culture, nature, and community.

If this love-psychology of nature, collectivism, and ‘Saya Chongma' is adaptable to modern life, it will play a significant role in building a stress-free, balanced life for a self-respecting society.

title: AI Washing: A Conceptual Exploration

detail.title: AI Washing: A Conceptual Exploration
detail.abstract: This paper introduces and explores the concept of AI washing, a phenomenon where companies misrepresent or exaggerate their artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities to enhance marketing appeal and gain a competitive advantage. Despite its increasing prevalence, AI washing has received limited theoretical attention. Drawing on literature from similar practices, this paper develops a conceptual framework and typology to categorize various forms of AI washing. Theoretical implications include extending marketing ethics frameworks and existing theories to the domain of AI. The paper also highlights avenues for future empirical research, particularly in validating the proposed typology and exploring the consequences of AI washing on trust and brand reputation. From a practical standpoint, the paper offers recommendations for businesses to adopt more transparent AI marketing strategies and calls for regulatory interventions to mitigate the risks of AI washing. Finally, it discusses limitations and directions for further study.

title: Beyond Credentials: Qualitative Skills Mismatch in Korea's Youth Labor Market -A Theoretical Framework and Research Agenda

detail.title: Beyond Credentials: Qualitative Skills Mismatch in Korea's Youth Labor Market -A Theoretical Framework and Research Agenda
detail.abstract: Korea's youth labor market exhibits a striking paradox: one of the world's highest rates of tertiary educational attainment coexists with elevated youth unemployment and NEET rates, early job turnover, widespread employer complaints about skill gaps, and a growing population of highly educated "resting youth." While quantitative mismatch (over-education and field-of-study mismatch) has received substantial scholarly attention, this paper argues that a deeper qualitative skills mismatch remains undertheorized, poorly measured, and inadequately addressed in both academic research and practical interventions. Drawing on self-discrepancy theory and synthesizing verified secondary data from KOSTAT Economically Active Population Surveys, KRIVET Korean Education and Employment Panel (KEEP) waves 2016-2024, NYPI/KEIS Youth Panels, and OECD Education at a Glance 2024-2025, this study proposes the 4-Dimensional Qualitative Skills Mismatch Framework (4D-QSMF). The framework conceptualizes mismatch as an interpersonal gap between the credential-based "ideal/own" self that youth present and the heterogeneous, dynamic competencies that employers actually desire. The four interacting dimensions are: Epistemic (knowledge content and application gaps), Relational (social capital, networks, and signaling channel gaps), Temporal (timing, sequencing, and skill-updating gaps), and Motivational (aspiration-reality alignment and incentive gaps). This paper does not report new primary data collection. All empirical illustrations derive from transparent secondary analyses of official datasets. The theoretical contribution lies in foregrounding the interpersonal and configurational nature of qualitative mismatch. The design and policy contribution provides concrete, multi-level intervention proposals, including measurement tools, platform features (augmentation and assemblage logics), and policy toolkits explicitly mapped to each dimension. A detailed 4-stage measurement development protocol and a 5-phase future empirical validation program are presented to enable rigorous testing. The research agenda outlines seven high-priority studies designed to generate citable findings across labor economics, vocational psychology, and information systems. By treating qualitative mismatch as a designable rather than inevitable feature of school-to-work transitions, Korea-and other high-education, rapidly transforming economies-can move beyond credential accumulation toward genuine skill alignment, enhanced youth agency, and more efficient, equitable labor market matching.

detail.abstract: Service businesses are increasingly facing more demanding customers as a result of a shift in power from the service providers' side to the customers' side. Related literature predominantly examines the negative side of this ongoing trend, while overlooking the positive side. The major aim of this paper is to examine how frontline employeesinvestment account managersdeal with the ongoing increase in customer demandingness. To address this, we draw on adaptability performance theory to test the facilitating effect of frontline employees' post-transaction service behaviors (SBs)-diligence, inducements, information communication, sportsmanship, and empathyas a means of adaptation to higher levels of customer demand. Findings indicate that frontline employees adapt most of their SBs' intensities to match customers' demands. The results show that some SBs actually increase the effectiveness and efficiency of frontline employees' service performance, leading to an increase in customer value and satisfaction. Customer value is found as a mediator in some of the relationships between SBs and customer satisfaction. Contrary to the conception of the negative outcomes of customer demandingness, service firms need to consider taking advantage of customer demandingness by stressing the role of frontline employees in adapting to customers' demands.

title: Slowing Down AI with IP
affiliations: University of Richmond School of Law and

detail.title: Slowing Down AI with IP

publicationDetails.detailsText: GWU Legal Studies Research Paper Forthcoming
publicationDetails.journalName: George Washington University Law School Legal Studies Research Paper Series

detail.abstract:
The current artificial intelligence (AI) landscape is defined by “too much, too fast”: rapid, winner-take-all scaling by a handful of firms, backed by states and capital markets, with little transparency into training data, model architectures, or deployment practices. The resulting harms are widely recognized: environmental damage, labor displacement, economic instability, privacy violations, and perpetuation of bias.

What is not widely recognized is the role that intellectual property (IP) can play in mitigating these harms. Existing policy debates largely treat IP protection as an AI accelerant, framing patent and copyright as incentives for more and faster AI innovation. If this were true, granting IP rights to AI innovators would only make things worse. But this Article inverts the conventional framing. When it comes to AI development, IP’s incentive effect is minimal, whereas IP’s well-known costs—e.g., reduced production, slower diffusion, and mandatory disclosure—predominate.

Maintaining and expanding IP protection for AI technologies therefore has the opposite of its usual effect: it slows down innovation. This makes it a uniquely fitting regulatory tool for the “too much, too fast” AI landscape. And while IP is by no means a cure-all, it has unexpected advantages over more common regulatory strategies. Overall, we reposition IP not as fuel for the AI race, but as a necessary brake on a runway industry.

title: Revisiting Wage and Price Inflation in the UK: Evidence from the Covid-19 era
affiliations: University of Greenwich

detail.title: Revisiting Wage and Price Inflation in the UK: Evidence from the Covid-19 era
detail.abstract: This paper examines the role of the labour market in the UK's post-pandemic inflation episode, focusing on two questions: whether wages pass through to prices, and what drives nominal wage growth. Conceptualizing wage pressure as arising from two channels of bargaining power-an individual channel operating through job-to-job mobility and labour market tightness, and a collective channel operating through unionised industrial action-I use local projections on aggregate UK data to estimate the pass-through of wages to headline, core, and services inflation, and to identify the drivers of wage growth. I find that the wage-price pass-through is modest, concentrated in the private sector, and most robust for services inflation; contrary to expectations, labour market tightness does not amplify this pass-through, and the transmission weakened rather than strengthened after 2020. Individual bargaining power, proxied by the quit rate, is a strong and robust predictor of wage growth, consistent with the job-ladder hypothesis, while collective bargaining power, proxied by industrial action, matters only in the highly unionised public sector. These results suggest that, despite historically elevated labour market tightness, wages cannot be regarded as a major driver of the UK's post-pandemic inflation or its persistence, with implications for how monetary policymakers should weigh labour market conditions in setting interest rates.

title: Future Value Theory: A Management Framework for Enterprise, Capital, and Society in the Age of AI

detail.title: Future Value Theory: A Management Framework for Enterprise, Capital, and Society in the Age of AI
detail.abstract: Future Value Theory is a management framework for the age of artificial intelligence. It argues that the primary purpose of an enterprise is not to maximize profit or enterprise value, but to continuously create Future Value-the capability to create value that does not yet exist. As AI democratizes knowledge, analysis, and execution, sustainable competitive advantage shifts from operational efficiency to the ability to define purpose, redefine the enterprise, allocate capital toward the future, and transform societal challenges into new markets. The paper develops an integrated set of constructs-Enterprise Redefinition, Future Capital, Human-on-the-Loop Management, Future Value Creation Capability, and the Future Value Economy-and expresses each as a multiplicative relationship in which purpose and trust are necessary conditions. Positioned as an extension of, rather than a replacement for, competitive strategy, stakeholder theory, disruptive innovation, and purpose-driven management, Future Value Theory reframes profit, enterprise value, and shareholder value as outcomes of a prior capacity to create the future. The framework is offered not as a theory for predicting the future, but as a set of first principles for creating it.

detail.abstract: As users increasingly rely on conversational AI assistants such as ChatGPT, Claude, and Perplexity for recommendations, information visibility is increasingly decided during the retrieval phase of retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines rather than on a traditional results page. This paper isolates and empirically tests the "Objectivity Premium": the hypothesis that factual, entity-style copy is retrieved more reliably than promotional, marketing-style copy for factual queries. We evaluate this hypothesis across a hybrid corpus: (1) a primary synthetic corpus of 80 fictional companies generated across three distinct language models with identical underlying facts, and (2) a corroborating real-web dataset of 40 companies (reducing to 29 complete pairs after auditing for scraping gaps). Evaluating retrieval proximity across two open-source sentence-embedding models (all-MiniLM-L6-v2 and all-mpnet-base-v2) against 1,200 queries, our clean synthetic test confirms the premium for factual queries (79.0% to 84.0% win rates) and its collapse to near-chance (~56.5% to 57.5%) under promotional-register queries. The real-web corpus directionally corroborates the premium (70.3% to 87.6% win rates), though it remains subject to a structural Wikipedia-vs-homepage confound. We discuss the implications for machine-legible web design and provide full replication protocols.

Between Agency and the Crisis of Meaning -A Proposal for a New Existential Category
detail.abstract: This article introduces the concept of the 'Promise Generation' as a new analytical category in social philosophy and organizational sociology. The category describes a collectivity of individuals-approximately 31-55 years of age-who entered adulthood and professional life under conditions of four cultural promises: agency, meaning, stability, and dialogue. The collision with reality-technological transformation, multigenerational organizational structures, and social acceleration-has led to a crisis of self-narrative that cannot be described by existing concepts: neither professional burnout, nor midlife crisis, nor economic depression. This category is not synonymous with the concept of Millennials-it is an existential and philosophical category based on the structure of experience, not on date of birth. Crucially, we do not call this category the 'Generation of Disillusionment', because disillusionment describes an emotional effect, while promise describes the constitutive structure of identity. This article is a seed for a broader research project aimed at empirical verification of the proposed category and the development of a new paradigm for generational categorization based on the structure of experience, not on date of birth.

title: Evaluating and Enhancing a Campus Ministry Program using Appreciative Inquiry

detail.title: Evaluating and Enhancing a Campus Ministry Program using Appreciative Inquiry
detail.abstract: This study evaluates the Campus Ministry Program of Mount Carmel College using Appreciative Inquiry as a framework for program evaluation and realignment. Anchored in qualitative action research, the study examined the program's strengths, core life-giving factors, and areas for improvement based on the perspectives of 56 participants, including students, coordinators, and administrators. The Appreciative Inquiry 4-D Cycle (Discover, Dream, Design, and Destiny) was utilized to identify existing strengths and generate strategies for program enhancement. Findings revealed that the program is generally functional and contributes to students' spiritual growth and personal development, particularly through operational activities such as retreats, practices, and exposure-based opportunities. However, leadership consistency, structured orientation, and member engagement were identified as areas needing improvement. The core life-giving factors valued by the youth include positive influence and community service, highlighting the program's role in values formation and social responsibility. The study further identified actionable strategies such as strengthening leadership, improving orientation programs, enhancing youth-centered activities, and expanding community outreach initiatives. Sustainability of the program was found to depend on strong leadership commitment, active participation, continuous evaluation, and institutional support. The study concludes with the development of an enhanced Campus Ministry Program that is more responsive to contemporary youth needs, promoting holistic formation, community engagement, and values-driven leadership. The findings provide a basis for program improvement and offer insights for similar faith-based educational institutions.

title: Resolving the Merger Paradoxes: Macro-monetary Shocks, Cost of Capital Divergence, and the Corporate Control Cycle (1985-2025)

detail.title: Resolving the Merger Paradoxes: Macro-monetary Shocks, Cost of Capital Divergence, and the Corporate Control Cycle (1985-2025)
detail.abstract:
This paper introduces a Unifying Theoretical Paradigm to resolve the historical value destruction, wave synchronicity, and post-wave de-consolidation paradoxes that have fragmented the corporate control literature for decades. Moving away from behavioral assumptions of managerial hubris or market irrationality, we model the aggregate wave-like clustering of mergers and acquisitions (M&A) as a rational response to systemic macro-monetary shifts. Using a comprehensive dataset of U.S. nonfinancial corporate transactions spanning from 1985 to 2025, estimated strictly in stationary first differences (Delta) under heteroskedasticity-robust Newey-West estimators, we uncover an asymmetric asset-pricing transmission channel.

Our empirical findings demonstrate that an exogenous elevation in short-term risk-free rates (Delta TB3_t > 0) triggers a counterintuitive fiscal wealth effect within the sovereign debt maturity structure. At T-bill redemption, a predictable nominal liquidity injection flushes into the commercial banking sector, expanding corporate credit supply and depressing private lending rates for prime borrowers. Mega-cap corporate entities exploit this unique window of depressed lending rates alongside a compressed Earnings-to-Price (E/P) ratio. This market compression operationalizes a negative first-order partial derivative of their marginal cost of capital (1 - Beta_Big < 0), rendering large-firm financing exceptionally cheap. Conversely, lower-beta targets experience an escalation in investor return requirements (1 - Beta_Small > 0), compressing their contemporary market valuations and generating a lucrative structural discount.

Corporate executives and controlling boards sequentially exploit this asymmetric capital cost divergence to execute high-premium defensive mergers, converting volatile nominal bank liquidity into real-sector tangible scale to lock in Beta and protect managerial tenure. Finally, our distributed lag specifications capture a two-year cyclical harmonic monetary reversal (rho2 = -0.5790), proving that trailing post-wave corporate spin-offs and asset divestitures represent a calculated mechanism of balance-sheet cleansing once the aggregate macro-monetary pendulum contracts.

detail.abstract: This technical note defines the Exponentially Biased Debt Repayment Weight, a closed-form method for ranking indebted users from repayment history. Each repayment is normalized by a fixed reference debt amount and weighted by an exponential recency function, producing a transparent score that emphasizes recent repayment behavior while retaining a controlled contribution from older history. title: Transforming Urban Futures: A Comprehensive Analysis of Artificial Intelligence Applications in Urban Planning and Smart City Development

detail.title: Transforming Urban Futures: A Comprehensive Analysis of Artificial Intelligence Applications in Urban Planning and Smart City Development
detail.abstract: The accelerating pace of global urbanisation has placed unprecedented pressure on city infrastructure, governance, and resource management systems. Traditional urban planning methodologies, largely developed in the twentieth century, are becoming insufficient to address complex, interconnected urban challenges, including traffic congestion, pollution, energy inefficiency, and inequitable public-service delivery. This paper presents a rigorous examination of the multifaceted impact of Artificial Intelligence (AI) on urban planning and smart-city development. We systematically analyse the enabling technology stack-comprising Machine Learning (ML), Deep Learning (DL), the Internet of Things (IoT), Big Data Analytics, Geographic Information Systems (GIS), and Digital Twins-that collectively forms the backbone of intelligent urban ecosystems. AI application domains investigated include adaptive traffic signal control, demand-responsive waste collection, smart-grid energy optimisation, water-network anomaly detection, predictive public safety, AI-assisted healthcare dispatch, and environmental airquality forecasting. Drawing on documented case studies from Singapore, Barcelona, Dubai, and Indian cities under the Smart Cities Mission, we evaluate the real-world effectiveness and scalability of AI-driven urban solutions, synthesising quantitative performance benchmarks across deployments. A structured analysis of challenges-encompassing algorithmic bias, surveillance ethics, cybersecurity vulnerabilities, digital inequality, and fiscal barriers-is presented alongside mitigation frameworks. The paper concludes with a forward-looking perspective on emerging paradigms including autonomous vehicles, generative AI in urban design, AI-powered Digital Twin operating systems, 6Genabled ultra-dense sensing, Green AI, and quantum-accelerated optimisation. We argue that ethically responsible and inclusive AI implementation, grounded in transparent data governance, is essential for cities that are not only intelligent but also equitable, resilient, and sustainable.

title: Rethinking The Work Product Doctrine For The AI Era: Why Matters More Than Who Or When
affiliations: University of Miami - School of Law

detail.title: Rethinking The Work Product Doctrine For The AI Era: Why Matters More Than Who Or When
detail.abstract:
Lawyers worldwide now routinely rely on generative and agentic AI tools—general-purpose tools like Claude and ChatGPT and legal platforms like Harvey, Legora, and CoCounsel—to analyze transactions, assess risk, draft documents, and shape legal advice. Drawing on 50 interviews with senior in-house lawyers, partners, legal-operations leaders, and corporate executives, this Article demonstrates that AI is already embedded in legal work. Yet whether the work product doctrine protects these materials remains unresolved. Five decisions from 2024-2026 frame the debate. United States v. Heppner, 820 F. Supp. 3d 292, 294 (S.D.N.Y. 2026) held that documents a criminal defendant generated using an open, consumer AI platform were not privileged or protected as work product. Warner v. Gilbarco, Inc., 820 F. Supp. 3d (E.D. Mich. Feb. 10, 2026) reached the opposite conclusion, holding that AI-assisted litigation materials constitute protected work product and that treating AI tools as third parties for waiver purposes would "nullify work-product protection in nearly every modern drafting environment." Morgan v. V2X, Inc. (D. Colo. Mar. 30, 2026) substantially extended Warner, analogizing AI to email, phones, and smart devices, and introduced AI-specific protective order language. Two earlier cases in the Northern District of California, Tremblay v. OpenAI, Inc. and Concord Music Group, Inc. v. Anthropic PBC, had already held that AI prompts crafted by counsel reflect mental impressions and litigation strategy i.e., opinion work product that is virtually undiscoverable.  However, the critical unresolved question is how courts will and should apply the work product doctrine going forward. 

In addition to recommending that parties and attorneys use closed, confidential AI systems whenever possible to ensure work product protection, this Article makes three main arguments. First, who prepared the work product shouldn't matter. Attorney involvement or direction should not be required. The focus should be on the “why” not the “who” especially since there will be AI-generated content that is not created by any person per se.

Second, the anticipation of litigation requirement is construed too narrowly and unequally as related when the duty of preservation begins. Ironically, when the courts are determining when the duty of preservation of documents begins it is based on a much broader interpretation of the anticipation of litigation. In work product, some courts demand a unilateral belief that is more than probable and also that the litigation is imminent or impending in time. Therefore, potential parties who use AI for legal research before the anticipation of litigation requirement is met, have no protection under the work product doctrine. As such, they are creating discoverable records that can establish corporate knowledge, willfulness, and scienter. Recent cybersecurity cases demonstrate how the "anticipation" requirement fails even when litigation is probable. Applied to AI, this gap is magnified because AI creates comprehensive, timestamped logs of every query. However, when applying the duty of preservation, courts only require that there be a reasonable good faith that litigation is credibly probable (regardless of when). Therefore, this Article recommends the courts use the same standard as in the preservation requirement along with a why analysis (whether because of or primary purpose) instead of the currently narrow when analysis applied.

Third, the ordinary course of business exception is too broad and, given the way AI is used today, should be eliminated. My prior article on the subject argued that the ordinary course of business exception enables courts to deny protection by infusing their narrow view of the corporate attorney's role into the analysis thereby making the distinction between "business" and "law" outcome-determinative.  For AI, this problem is existential: as AI becomes the ordinary course of business for law firms and legal departments (and it already is for many), the exception threatens to swallow the rule entirely. If every legal department and law firm uses AI daily for everything—contract review, regulatory research, risk assessment—then all AI-assisted work product could be characterized as "ordinary course of business." Therefore, this Article concludes that the recommendation of my prior article to eliminate the business/law distinction from the work product analysis applies with even greater force to AI, where the distinction has gone from "arbitrary and impossible" to unworkable because the same tool, in the same session, can perform both legal and business analysis.

detail.title: Targeted Repression and Political Repertoire Compression: Evidence from the Ansei Purge in Japan
detail.abstract: This paper studies whether targeted repression changes not only the level but also the composition of recorded political activity. I examine the Ansei Purge of 1858-1860 in Japan, when coercive enforcement focused on politically salient networks during the treaty and succession crisis. Overt political activity exposed political ties to regime scrutiny, while learning and training activity could operate through less public capability networks. I assemble a monthly prefecture panel from the Historiographical Institute's Summary database of the Ishin Shiryō and separate visible movement-side mobilization from lower-visibility knowledge building. The design interacts the October 1858 enforcement onset with source-side Ii-family political visibility and a combined measure of pre-1858 Westernlearning and medical-learning capacity. Visible movement-side activity contracts where both exposures are high, while knowledge-building activity does not rise in parallel: the shift toward knowledge-side activity reflects fewer mobilization records, not more knowledge production. Placebo timing, negative-control outcomes, exposure-definition variants, permutation inference, and phase-based sensitivity checks confirm this timing and movement-side pattern. The evidence indicates that targeted coercion changed which forms of political activity remained visible, without eliminating the underlying capability networks.

detail.abstract: The dominant paradigm of corporate strategy in consolidated, regulated service industries has operated on a durable premise: scale wins. Larger organizations, with deeper balance sheets, broader referral networks, and superior purchasing power, were assumed to possess structural competitive advantages that smaller, more agile competitors could not overcome. This premise is failing. A structural shift — the convergence of hyper-localized geographic competition, assetlight operational models, and governed artificial intelligence deployment — is creating a new competitive dynamic in which velocity of market entry and depth of digital integration generate competitive advantages that raw corporate scale cannot replicate and frequently cannot respond to in time. This paper introduces the Capital-Efficiency Trilemma: a structural governance constraint in consolidated industry strategy that formalizes three simultaneously non-negotiable competitive dimensions — deployment velocity, capital efficiency, and trust-based governance — as structurally interdependent variables resistant to sequential optimization. Derived from the same macroeconomic structural logic that grounds the AIconomics Trilemma in organizational AI governance, the Capital-Efficiency Trilemma establishes that organizations in consolidated markets cannot simultaneously maximize speed-to-market, capital efficiency, and trustgovernance integrity under conventional capital-heavy expansion models, and that the failure to recognize this structural constraint produces characteristic, predictable competitive failure modes. The paper introduces the OTR Framework — Outpace, Trust, Resilience — as the operational model for navigating the Trilemma, the Market-Timing Paradox as the empirical mechanism through which legacy scale converts from competitive advantage to competitive liability, and the 5:1 Capital Investment Discipline as the bridge connecting the Capital-Efficiency Trilemma to the AIconomics organizational governance frameworks published in prior work. The paper is grounded in publicly available empirical data on industry consolidation dynamics and is positioned as a practitioner-scholar contribution at the intersection of competitive strategy, industrial organization economics, and enterprise AI governance. Six testable propositions establish an empirical research agenda.

detail.title: Recognizing What's Around the Corner: Merger Control, Capabilities, and the New Nature of Potential Competition
detail.abstract: This paper argues for a capabilities-based, forward-looking approach to merger control that reflects the realities of dynamic competition. In fast-evolving sectors, the most significant competitive threats often come not from current rivals but from de novo firms or adjacent firms developing complementary technologies or capabilities. Conventional antitrust tools — rooted in static market shares and product overlaps — fail to detect these latent challengers or assess the innovation potential of mergers. We draw on economic theory, executive insight, and case studies (Meta–Giphy, Adobe–Figma, Amazon–iRobot) to show how competitive uncertainty disciplines incumbents and how mergers can either suppress or amplify that dynamic. We propose a framework that shifts the focus from products to capabilities: assessing technological assets, organizational routines, and innovation trajectories. This approach reduces enforcement errors — both false positives and false negatives — and enables regulators to protect long-term rivalry without undermining legitimate adaptation to new technology and market shifts By recognizing unseen competition as a structural feature of dynamic markets, and by evaluating mergers through the lens of capabilities, agencies can better align merger control with the goal of promoting sustained innovation and longer-term consumer welfare.

title: Exploring The Role of Digital Tools in Facilitating Business Development: A Case Study of Rigworld Group in the Oil And Gas Manpower Service Sector in Ghana

detail.title: Exploring The Role of Digital Tools in Facilitating Business Development: A Case Study of Rigworld Group in the Oil And Gas Manpower Service Sector in Ghana
detail.abstract: The digital transformation of business operations has become imperative for competitive advantage in the oil and gas industry, yet limited empirical evidence exists on how manpower service providers in emerging markets leverage digital tools for business development. This study explores the role of digital tools in facilitating business development within Ghana's oil and gas manpower services sector, focusing on Rigworld Group as a case study. Guided by the Technology-Organization-Environment framework, the study employed a qualitative research approach with twenty participants purposively selected from various departments including business development, human resources, operations, finance, and information technology. Data was collected through semi-structured interviews lasting 45 to 75 minutes and analyzed using thematic analysis to identify patterns related to digital tool adoption. The findings revealed that Customer Relationship Management systems maintained client relationship continuity but faced inconsistent departmental adoption and training gaps. Enterprise Resource Planning systems effectively integrated procurement, finance, and operations despite change resistance and system rigidity. Data analytics tools showed significant potential for strategic decision-making but remained underutilized due to restricted access and absence of a data-driven culture. E-recruitment platforms successfully expanded the talent pool and accelerated hiring processes but suffered from inefficient candidate filtering and poor integration with other HR systems. The study concludes that while Rigworld Group has progressed in digital adoption, a fragmented approach characterized by departmental silos, inadequate training, and poor system integration limits the full realization of digital transformation benefits. It is recommended that the company implement comprehensive training programs, establish clear usage protocols across departments, foster a data-first organizational culture, and form a dedicated cross-functional team to spearhead an integrated digital transformation strategy that aligns technology adoption with strategic business objectives.

detail.abstract: Purpose: Employee turnover is a persistent challenge for early-stage ventures, yet most research on this problem draws on samples from mature firms in developed economies. This paper addresses a narrower and largely unexamined context: student-led entrepreneurial teams operating within university-based startup ecosystems in Egypt. Drawing on job embeddedness theory, the paper develops a conceptual model explaining why members of such teams form the intention to stay or the intention to leave, and proposes founder-team relationship quality as a boundary condition on this relationship. title: Spatial Spillover and Synergistic Effects of Leading Pedestrian Intervals: Empirical Evidence from New York City

detail.title: Spatial Spillover and Synergistic Effects of Leading Pedestrian Intervals: Empirical Evidence from New York City
detail.abstract: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI) is a signal-timing treatment designed to reduce pedestrian-vehicle conflicts at signalized intersections, yet conventional evaluations often assume intersection-level independence and overlook heterogeneity in traffic exposure. Using a panel of 36,018 intersection-year observations from New York City between 2013 and 2018, this study combines multidimensional coarsened exact matching with a high-dimensional fixed-effects Poisson pseudo-maximum likelihood model and cluster-robust standard errors. The estimated effects vary with traffic state and spatial deployment pattern. Under low-to-moderate traffic volumes, LPI is associated with local safety gains and protective spillovers to adjacent intersections. Under high-volume conditions, isolated LPI is associated with risk transfer to adjacent intersections, consistent with compressed vehicular right-of-way. Clustered LPI deployments appear to attenuate this adverse spillover, suggesting a network-level traffic-calming effect. Model-based counterfactual topology reconstruction indicates that, under the same number of installed LPIs, reallocating treatments could increase avoided crashes by 52.97%, reduce the spatial standard deviation of residual risk by 4.70%, and lower maximum intersection risk by 8.71%. These model-based findings show that LPI programs should be evaluated and deployed as network-level interventions rather than as isolated intersection treatments.

title: Risk-Informed Heterogeneous Proxy Models Using Machine Learning to Predict Cool-Down Time for Hydrate Mitigation in Deepwater Petroleum Pipelines

detail.title: Risk-Informed Heterogeneous Proxy Models Using Machine Learning to Predict Cool-Down Time for Hydrate Mitigation in Deepwater Petroleum Pipelines
detail.abstract: After an unplanned shutdown in subsea oil and gas pipelines, hydrate-formation risk can increase rapidly, potentially leading to blockage, delayed restart, and escalation of process-safety and flowassurance consequences. Operators must estimate the Cool-Down Time (CDT) rapidly because this time window constrains the preservation actions that can be safely executed before hydrate-favourable pressure-temperature conditions are reached. As an alternative to computationally demanding multiphase-flow simulations, this paper develops a risk-informed Heterogeneous Composite Proxy (HCP) model for fast CDT prediction using operating conditions measured at the onset of shutdown. The proposed framework combines a cost-sensitive binary classifier, which identifies high-and low-risk operating regimes with respect to a CDT threshold, with two local regression models dedicated to the corresponding regimes. An Adaptive Hybrid Sampling (AHS) procedure is then used to enrich the training set both near the risk boundary and inside the high-risk region, where prediction errors have the most severe operational consequences. The framework is evaluated on an OLGA-based model of a real offshore pipeline and compared with global and composite proxy baselines trained with conventional and adaptive sampling. The results show that the proposed risk-informed HCP improves CDT prediction in the high-risk region while maintaining online prediction times compatible with operational decision support.

title: Warranted AI: Seven Conditions for Defensible Reliance on Consequential AI-Enabled Decisions and Actions in Regulated Industries

detail.abstract:
Organisations already rely on AI-enabled decisions and actions in consequential settings. Yet accountability has not kept pace with technology. Warranted Reliance means reliance that can be justified, defended and stood behind with accountability. The key gap is that governance intent is not the same as Governance in Effect. Policies, approvals, inventories and assurance reports alone do not show that governance operated when a system shaped a decision, initiated an action or produced consequences.

Warranted AI addresses that gap by defining a Warranting Standard for organisational reliance on consequential AI-enabled decisions and actions. It is a threshold test for when reliance can be justified, defended and stood behind. This is not an AI ethics framework, a model explainability method or a compliance checklist. Warranted AI defines the conditions under which reliance can be warranted.

The standard takes the form of seven conditions that operate together. They test whether the organisation knew what it relied on, could trace what occurred, preserved accountability, enforced boundaries, sustained scrutiny, maintained independent oversight and protected the context and state required for reliance. The standard is sector-agnostic because institutional forms differ, but the reliance question does not.

Warranted AI is not proof of legality. It is the evidentiary condition for defensible organisational reliance.
